# BAD-002 — iOS App Store rejection (2026-09-14): guest mode with optional sign-in, ads and in-app purchases unlinked, and the reply to App Review

## Brief
App Review rejected Bad Takes iOS 1.0 (build 13003, submission af7a491a-ca33-47bb-aeb6-44c6fc065230, reviewed 2026-09-14 on an iPad Air 11-inch M3, iPadOS 27.0) for three reasons:

1. Guideline 5.1.1(v): the app requires sign-in before accessing scenes. Apps may require registration only for account-based features.
2. Guideline 2.1: the binary uses AppTrackingTransparency, and the reviewer could not find the ATT prompt. Either show it with a device screen recording, or stop tracking and update App Privacy to declare no tracking.
3. Guideline 2.1(b): the app may give access to paid digital content. Apple asks who uses it, where it is bought, what previously purchased content is reachable in the app, and what is unlocked without in-app purchase.

Eric's decisions (2026-09-14):
- Guest mode with optional sign-in. A signed-out user can play a scene but cannot download or install one from the hosted catalog, because that runs on Bad Takes' backend and anonymous use should not spend it. Sign-in stays for account-based features. Eric asked that this line be checked against Apple's guidelines before it is built.
- Ads and in-app purchases are out of the iOS build for the first approval: unlink the AdMob and RevenueCat plugins, strip the ATT usage string, the AdMob app id and SKAdNetworkItems from Info.plist, and keep the web-side ads and billing code dormant for later. Every mention of a paid plan (Plus, lifetime, ad-free, Remove ads, subscriptions) disappears from the iOS app. The desktop's paid licence stays, but it unlocks nothing on iOS.

Deliverables: one BadTakes PR carrying the iOS-only code changes, updated docs/MOBILE-STORES.md, a design note with the guideline analysis, and a drafted App Review reply plus review notes for Eric to paste. The App Store Connect changes are Eric's: App Privacy with no tracking, detaching the subscriptions, age-rating answers, and the reply itself.

## Size, persona and model decision
Three members, one PR. A researcher (fable, expensive if wrong: a wrong guideline read costs another review cycle) checks Eric's proposed guest scope against the App Review Guidelines and drafts the reply, in parallel with an engineer (opus) who unlinks AdMob and RevenueCat from the iOS shell and hides every plan, ad and subscription surface on iOS. A second engineer (opus) builds guest mode once the research settles the scope and the first engineer's web/ edits have returned, so their paths never overlap.
